rules.card.title: Expedition card
rules.card.purpose: Each Expedition card references a place represented by a green circle on the board.
rules.card.deck:
The deck contains {number, plural, one{# Expedition card} other{# Expedition cards}}.
You can use a ticket to draw 2 cards from the deck, discard one of them, then discard another card.
rules.card.hand.private:
This card is in your hand, it is a secret objective. You must take one of the 3 expeditions through this place on the board to achieve this objective and score 1 point.
If the objective is not reached, at the end of the game you will lose 1 point.
rules.card.hand.revealed:
This card is in your hand, but was revealed to the other players when you placed a token on the corresponding green circle. You must take one of the 3 expeditions through this place on the board to complete this objective and score 2 points (1 for the card and 1 for the token).
If the objective is not reached, at the end of the game you will lose 2 points (1 for the card and 1 for the token).
rules.card.hand.place.token: You may <0>put a token on this place</0>. This objective will be revealed, but will earn 2 points.
rules.card.hand.other: This card is a secret objective in {player}'s hand.
rules.card.common: This card is a common objective. The first player to take an expedition through this place on the board scores 1 point.
rules.ticket.title: A Ticket
rules.ticket.mine: You have {number, plural, one{# ticket} other{# tickets}}.
rules.ticket.other: {player} has {number, plural, one{# ticket} other{# tickets}}.
rules.ticket.purpose:
A player may use up to 2 tickets during his turn. Each ticket can be used before and/or after his expedition progress action.

<0>One ticket provides one additional action from the following 3:</0>

• Place an additional arrow from any expedition.
The player can extend the expedition of his choice (so same power as the blue square).

• Remove the last arrow of an expedition of choice
The player removes the last arrow of an expedition of his choice. If this allows a player to reach an objective, he can announce it and put the card in front of him face up. If the modified expedition leads to a blue square or red star, the player receives the associated bonus (new arrow or ticket).

• Exchange an Expedition card
The player can exchange one of his Expedition cards in his hand for a new card from the deck. To do this, he draws 2 cards from the deck, chooses one of the 2 cards and places it in his hand, then places the other one back under the deck along with the card he wishes to discard from his hand.
rules.arrow.stock.yellow: There {stock, plural, one{is # yellow arrow} other{are # yellow arrows}} in stock.
rules.arrow.stock.blue: There {stock, plural, one{is # blue arrow} other{are # blue arrows}} in stock.
rules.arrow.stock.red: There {stock, plural, one{is # red arrow} other{are # red arrows}} in stock.
rules.arrow.purpose:
The arrows represent the progress of the 3 expeditions on the board.
The expeditions do not belong to any player, they are common to all players. They always start from the starting point (compass rose).
rules.token.title: {player}'s token
rules.token.purpose:
Each player has 4 tokens. These tokens are used to mark 4 player objectives at the beginning of the game.
If an expedition reaches a place marked with a token and the player still has that place in his hand, he places the card and the corresponding token on it, which scores 2 points at the end of the game (1 for the card and 1 for the token).
Each token still on the board at the end of the game loses 1 point.
rules.largeToken.purpose: This token serves as a reminder of the player's color.
rules.board.title: The game board
rules.place.compass.title: Starting point
rules.board.place.compass: The starting point in Northern Europe is the compass rose, all expeditions will start from this point.
rules.board.place.green: The green circles are the 80 places for which there is a corresponding Expedition card.
rules.place.blue.title: Blue square
rules.board.place.blue: The blue squares are intermediate steps. When you bring an Expedition to a blue square, you can immediately place a new arrow to extend any Expedition.
rules.place.red.title: Red star
rules.board.place.red: The red stars are intermediate steps. When you bring an Expedition to a red star, you immediately get a <0>ticket</0>.
rules.place.red.border: This crossing point allows expeditions to cross to the other side of the board, at the same latitude.
rules.board.road: The dotted segments between 2 locations represent the routes that Expeditions can take by placing the arrows on them.
rules.place.arrow: Place a {color, select, 1{yellow} 2{blue} other{red}} arrow towards: {destination}
rules.place.token: Put a token on this place
rules.place.token.forbidden: You cannot place a token on a location within 3 segments of the starting point.
rules.place.common: This place is a common goal for all players. The first player to bring an expedition here will score 1 point.
rules.place.hand: This place is in your hand. If any player brings an expedition here you will score 1 point.
rules.road.title: A road
rules.lastTurn.lastPlayer: The game ends at the end of {player}'s turn.
rules.lastTurn.text: The game ends when someone has placed the last Expedition card from their hand, or when all the arrows are on the map. Finish the round so everyone gets the same number of turns.
rules.score: You each count your own points:
rules.score.card:
<0>+1 point</0> for each card in front of you
(objective completed)
rules.score.token:
<0>+1 point</0> per token collected
(key location visited)
rules.malus.card: <0>-1 point</0> per Expedition card still in your hand
rules.malus.token: <0>-1 point</0> per token of your color still on the map
rules.winner:
The player with the most points wins.
If it’s a tie, the tied player with the most tickets wins.
If it’s still a tie, the tied players share the victory.

place.1.name: Svalbard
place.1.text: One of the best places to observe polar bears; today, there are 3,500 in the region.
place.2.name: Athens
place.2.text: It is the oldest European city, and the cradle of democracy. The name comes from Athena, protective goddess of the city, who knew how to stand up to Poseidon.
place.3.name: Rome
place.3.text: The Colosseum was the largest amphitheater in the Roman empire. With its ovoid shape and extraordinary dimensions, it can accommodate as many spectators as the Stade de France.
place.4.name: Stonehenge
place.4.text: Stonehenge is one of the most impressive prehistoric monuments in the world, due to the size of its megaliths, the complexity of its concentric plan, and its architectural design.
place.5.name: Thingvellir
place.5.text: Thingvellir National Park is one of Iceland’s most famous sites. From 930 to 1798, it housed the Althingi, considered to be the oldest parliament in Europe.
place.6.name: Zagorsk
place.6.text: The city is best known for its huge Orthodox monastery, founded in the 14th Century CE (Trinity Lavra of Saint Sergius), considered the heart of Russian Orthodoxy.
place.7.name: Caspian Sea
place.7.text: It is the largest closed sea in the world, bordered by 5 countries. Its large quantity of fish, especially sturgeon, makes it the leading caviar-producing region of the world.
place.8.name: Petra
place.8.text: Al-Khazneh, the most famous of the monuments in the city, is believed to be the tomb of a king or queen, and was long the target of attacks by Bedouins who thought they’d find some important treasure there.
place.9.name: Giza
place.9.text: In 1798, at the foot of the pyramids of Giza, Bonaparte pronounced decisively, “Think of it, soldiers: From the summit of these pyramids, forty centuries look down upon you.”
place.10.name: Timgad
place.10.text: Founded by Trajan in 100 CE as a military colony, this ancient Roman city in Algeria is nicknamed “Pompeii of North Africa”.
place.11.name: Newfoundland
place.11.text: This large island became Canadian in 1949. Its capital, St. John’s, which is at the eastern end of the island, is the easternmost point in North America.
place.12.name: Greenland
place.12.text: It is the least densely populated country in the world, with just over 50,000 inhabitants in an area 4 times the size of France. The capital is Nuuk, and the statue of Hans Egede, its founder, watches over the city.
place.13.name: Putorana Plateau
place.13.text: This plateau is part of the Putorana Nature Reserve; its lakes and rivers belong to an ecosystem untouched by humans, and make it a protected territory.
place.14.name: Novosibirsk
place.14.text: Culture in this city in Western Siberia is considered very important, including the Opera and Ballet Theater, the largest in Russia.
place.15.name: Babylon
place.15.text: The Lion of Babylon is a statue made of black basalt. It was discovered at the site in 1876, and is an important symbol of Mesopotamia that is used by several Iraqi organizations.
place.16.name: Persepolis
place.16.text: This former capital of Persia was constructed under Darius I around 500 BCE. The Gate of All Nations, built by his son Xerxes, is one of the major remains of the ancient city.
place.17.name: Sanaa
place.17.text: An artistic and architectural masterpiece, this city has been inhabited for more than 3,000 years, and today still has 106 mosques and 3,500 houses dating from before the 11th Century CE.
place.18.name: Aksum
place.18.text: According to archaeologists, the Aksumite stelae mark the sites of the tombs of Aksumite rulers. Their empire was an important state in the Horn of Africa from the 1st through 4th Century CE.
place.19.name: Sahara
place.19.text: The Sahara has 20% sandy surfaces and 80% rocky surfaces. It gets 5 to 10 mm of rain per year, which makes it the driest region in the world.
place.20.name: Timbuktu
place.20.text: Founded in the 5th Century CE, this Malian city is full of mosques and mausoleums to perpetuate the memory of pious men, earning the city its nickname, “the city of 333 saints”.
place.21.name: Canary Islands
place.21.text: This archipelago, located off the coast of Morocco, is composed of 7 main islands of volcanic origin. The last eruption of the volcano Cumbre Vieja occurred in September 2021.
place.22.name: Northwest Passage
place.22.text: The famous Northwest Passage allows ships to connect from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean. Since the 15th Century CE, numerous explorers have tried to traverse it with varying degrees of success.
place.23.name: Sakha
place.23.text: Recent studies of the Pleistocene Park, in the Sakha region, have made it possible to reconstruct the woolly mammoth’s food and uses of the Siberian steppe.
place.24.name: Harappa
place.24.text: Terracotta pottery is typical in this archaeological site of a Bronze-Age walled city that spanned the period of the Indus Valley civilization, or Harappan, named after the city.
place.25.name: Taj Mahal
place.25.text: The Muslim Mughal emperor Shah Jahan had this white marble mausoleum built in homage to his wife, Arjumand Banu Begum, who died giving birth to their fourteenth child.
place.26.name: Virunga
place.26.text: This national park is home to more than a thousand species of mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians, as well as a third of the world’s endangered mountain gorillas.
place.27.name: Kush
place.27.text: Meroë became the capital of the Kingdom of Kush in the 4th Century BCE (after Kerma and Napata). The pyramids found there are the sepulchers of deceased royalty.
place.28.name: Douala
place.28.text: In this economic capital of Cameroon, La Nouvelle Liberté statue in the Deido suburb, restored in 2007, is today considered the symbol of the city.
place.29.name: Elmina
place.29.text: São Jorge da Mina Castle, which was built by the Portuguese in 1482, was a commercial center on the Gold Coast before unfortunately becoming a hub for slave trade.
place.30.name: Niagara Falls
place.30.text: Comprising 3 waterfalls (Horseshoe Falls, American Falls, and Bridal Veil Falls), these form not only a major tourist attraction, but a source of hydroelectric energy.
place.31.name: Banff
place.31.text: Established in 1885, Banff National Park (listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site) is Canada’s oldest national park; it is among the most frequented in the world, thanks to its varied and sumptuous landscapes.
place.32.name: Kolyma
place.32.text: A major mining center in the 20th Century CE, this region had many forced labor camps, which were particularly feared by prisoners, due to the climate and working conditions.
place.33.name: Lake Baikal
place.33.text: 336 rivers flow into this lake, which represents the largest reservoir of fresh water on the planet. It has exceptional aquatic fauna, with more than 1,500 animal species.
place.34.name: Great Wall
place.34.text: Although it is the longest human construction, the legend that it is visible from the moon is false: Its width (equivalent to a highway) is too narrow!
place.35.name: Mount Everest
place.35.text: Nearly 6,000 people have successfully reached the summit at 8,848 m above sea level, including a 13-year-old boy, someone blind, a 73-year-old woman, and an 80-year-old man!
place.36.name: Bagan
place.36.text: Buddhists have made pilgrimages to this location for centuries. The site still has 2,834 monuments (temples, stupas, pagodas) today, but only a few dozen are maintained.
place.37.name: Sigiriya
place.37.text: An immense rock, 370 m high, dubbed “Lion Rock”. To reach the fortress of King Kassapa at its summit, you must climb more than 1,300 steps.
place.38.name: Victoria Falls
place.38.text: Among the most impressive waterfalls in the world. Situated on the Zambezi River, they are 1,700 m wide, and reach as high as 108 m.
place.39.name: Puerto Rico
place.39.text: An unincorporated territory of the United States; Christopher Columbus made it known to the world, naming it San Juan Bautista in honor of Saint John the Baptist. Today, San Juan is the name of its capital.
place.40.name: Louisiane
place.40.text: This state (sold by Napoleon to the United States in 1803) is known for its bayous: large extremely humid marshes formed by the Mississippi River Delta Basin.
place.41.name: Old Faithful
place.41.text: This geyser, situated in Yellowstone National Park, is one of the largest jets of hot water and steam in the world. Very hot water (90°C) shoots up to 50 m high every 88 minutes, on average.
place.42.name: Crater Lake
place.42.text: A lake that formed in a crater of the volcano Mount Mazama in Oregon, it is the deepest in the United States (592 m), and has water so clear that objects up to 37 m deep can be seen with the naked eye.
place.43.name: Mackenzie Delta
place.43.text: The Mackenzie is Canada’s longest river. It stays frozen about 5 months per year. The delta forms a 13,500 km² swamp, and shelters an important population of migratory birds.
place.44.name: Bering Strait
place.44.text: The 83 km wide strait separates Alaska from Russia, and was nicknamed the “Ice Curtain” during the Cold War. The two Diomede Islands form the strait, separated by 3 km; each belongs to one of the countries.
place.45.name: Amur River
place.45.text: The name Amur comes from a Mongolian dialect, and means “mud”. Its current name in Mongolian means “black river”. As its names suggest, this is a black and muddy river.
place.46.name: Mount Fuji
place.46.text: The sacred mountain (in reality made of 3 volcanoes) is a historical and cultural emblem in Japan. Its conical shape with perfect symmetry is linked to the last volcanic eruption in 1707.
place.47.name: Xi’an
place.47.text: The mausoleum of Emperor Qin hosts an array of nearly 8,000 life-size terracotta statues of soldiers and horses meant to protect the late emperor.
place.48.name: Angkor Vat
place.48.text: This temple, first dedicated to the god Vishnu, became a place of Buddhist worship at the end of the 12th Century CE. It is the largest religious monument in the world, and the best preserved in Angkor.
place.49.name: Madagascar
place.49.text: The isolation of the island has generated a very high rate of endemism in animal and plant species. Among the numerous unique species is a baobab that is emblematic of the island; it is a gigantic bottletree that can live for more than 2,000 years.
place.50.name: Omatako
place.50.text: A pair of mountains with an appearance similar to a pair of buttocks, which is precisely what they are named in Herero, the local language: Omatako.
place.51.name: Salvador de Bahia
place.51.text: Consisting of two parts, Upper Town and Lower Town, the traditional way to go from one to the other is to take the Lacerda Elevator, which was built in 1873, and is 72 m high.
place.52.name: Tikal
place.52.text: This city is one of the best known of the great Mayan cities, and is a major archaeological site in Central America. The heart of the city centers around a concentration of temples around the Great Plaza.
place.53.name: Teotihuacan
place.53.text: An archaeological site in the Valley of Mexico, this city was one of the largest cities in the world in its heyday (around 500 CE), with around 200,000 inhabitants.
place.54.name: Grand Canyon
place.54.text: “In the Grand Canyon, Arizona has a natural wonder which is in kind absolutely unparalleled throughout the rest of the world.” Theodore Roosevelt.
place.55.name: Denali
place.55.text: The highest summit in North America reaches 6,190 m. Long named Mount McKinley (1896–2015), Denali means “the tall one” in the Koyukon Athabaskan (Native Alaskan) language.
place.56.name: Sulawesi
place.56.text: The traditional houses of Tana Toraja have roofs reminiscent of the shape of buffalo horns, which are a sacred animal in the community, sacrificed during funeral ceremonies.
place.57.name: Borobudur
place.57.text: This Buddhist temple was built around 800 CE, then abandoned around 1100 for unknown reasons. Rediscovered in 1814, it took 200 men 2 months to update the monument.
place.58.name: Atlantic Ocean
place.58.text: From the 5th to the 15th Century CE, Europeans called it the Ocean Sea. Christopher Columbus, the first to cross the Atlantic in 1492, was nicknamed “the Admiral of the Ocean Sea”.
place.59.name: Iguazu Falls
place.59.text: These waterfalls are among the most impressive in the world, comprising 275 individual falls, and forming a front about 3 km long, 80% of which is in Argentina, 20% of which is in Brazil.
place.60.name: Marajó
place.60.text: Marajó Island is the largest coastal island in Brazil, and its local police do not use horses to patrol, but rather… water buffalo.
place.61.name: Angel Falls
place.61.text: This waterfall in Venezuela is the highest in the world (807 m), and owes its name to the aviator Jimmy Angel, who saw it in 1933 while panning for gold.
place.62.name: Galapagos Islands
place.62.text: This archipelago, composed of 127 islands, islets, and rocks (29 of which are large) was annexed by Ecuador in 1832. “Islas de los Galápagos” in Spanish means “Islands of the Giant Tortoises”.
place.63.name: Papua
place.63.text: Most of the country is on the island of New Guinea. It is essentially mountainous and covered with tropical forests, very dense with trees and vegetation.
place.64.name: Arnhem Land
place.64.text: This vast wild expanse is rich with aboriginal culture, and is one of the best fishing spots in the world. The didgeridoo, a traditional Australian musical instrument, was also born here.
place.65.name: Bungle Bungle Range
place.65.text: This unique, orange-colored formation is made up of a set of towers and beehive-shaped cones, with steep sides, and a surface streaked with gray bands.
place.66.name: Indian Ocean
place.66.text: Formerly known to Europe as the Eastern Ocean, and to China as the Western Ocean, it covers 20% of the globe. Most of the waters in this ocean are tropical, making it the warmest ocean on the planet.
place.67.name: Atacama
place.67.text: The Hand of the Desert in Chile is an 11 m tall sculpture created in 1992 by Chilean artist Mario Irarrázabal, which leaves the visitor free to make their own interpretation.
place.68.name: Aripuanã
place.68.text: The Aripuanã National Forest is still home to a few indigenous tribes, including the Surui, who call themselves Paiter, which means “real people, ourselves”.
place.69.name: Amazon Rainforest
place.69.text: 400 billion trees (13% of the trees on Earth) of 16,000 different species, as well as 14,000 species of other plants, 2,200 species of fish, 1,300 species of birds…. This is the largest reservoir of biodiversity in the world.
place.70.name: Pacific Ocean
place.70.text: It is the largest ocean on Earth, covering 1/3 of Earth’s surface, and larger than the surface of Mars. Its depth in places is as great as 10,000 m.
place.71.name: Great Barrier Reef
place.71.text: The coral that makes up the Great Barrier Reef is 18 million years old, and cannot live deeper than 30 m, because it needs sunlight to live.
place.72.name: Uluru
place.72.text: Uluru is an inselberg (isolated relief, hill, or small mountain, which significantly dominates a plain or plateau). The site is home to watering holes, caves, and cave paintings.
place.73.name: Perth
place.73.text: The Elizabeth Quay Bridge, at 22 m high, allows pedestrians and cyclists to cross the Swan River, and connects downtown Perth to the business district.
place.74.name: Graham Land
place.74.text: Graham Land is the least icy region of Antarctica, and is therefore home to numerous scientific bases.
place.75.name: Tierra Del Fuego
place.75.text: This archipelago was named by the first European explorers to arrive, who saw fires moving in the darkness; it was the indigenous people using fire for warmth.
place.76.name: Altiplano
place.76.text: This region, which has been inhabited for more than 10,000 years, extends over 4 countries, but most of it is in Bolivia. Its average altitude of 3,330 m makes it the 2nd highest inhabited region in the world (after the Tibetan plateau).
place.77.name: Machu Picchu
place.77.text: This ancient Incan city from the 15th Century CE perches atop a mountain more than 2,400 m above sea level (its name means “old mountain”). Access to it is by foot, and is subject to strict control.
place.78.name: Rapa Nui
place.78.text: This Polynesian island is the most isolated inhabited place in the world (the nearest inhabited island is more than 2,000 km away). It is known for its impressive statues (moai).
place.79.name: Tasmania
place.79.text: This island is separated from the Australian mainland by the Bass Strait. The Freycinet National Park is home to the famous Wineglass Bay and its heavenly beaches.
place.80.name: Fiordland National Park
place.80.text: This is the place with spectacular landscapes that Peter Jackson chose as the filming location for many scenes of his “The Lord of the Rings” film trilogy.
tuto.welcome:
Welcome!
You're about to learn how to play <0>Expeditions around the world</0>.
tuto.goal: Three expeditions set out from Europe to discover the world. You must get them to visit your objectives before those of the other players.
tuto.cards: Each player holds 12 cards. Here are yours.
tuto.place: These cards represent places to visit on the board. Each green location has a corresponding card.
tuto.circles: To simplify the game, in Game Park, your locations are surrounded by a circle in your color, which other players can't see.
tuto.common: The places circled in purple are objectives common to all players. They correspond to these 6 cards.
tuto.tokens: When setting up, you must reveal 4 of your objectives to the other players, by placing these tokens on them.
tuto.tokens.canary: Place your first token on the Canary Islands.
tuto.tokens.opponent: Your opponent has placed his first token on the Northwest Passage. Place your other 3 tokens wherever you like.
tuto.arrows:
Now that the set-up is complete, the game can begin!
On your turn, you must place an arrow to move one of the 3 expeditions forward.
tuto.start: The expeditions all start from the compass rose here.
tuto.rome: Place a yellow arrow here, to advance the yellow expedition to Rome.
tuto.pass: At the top of the screen, click "Pass" to end your turn.
tuto.blue.goto: Now it's your turn. Move the yellow expedition towards the blue square.
tuto.blue.replay: Bravo! Arriving on a blue square allows you to play again. Take the yellow expedition to the Canary Islands!
tuto.canary.score: You have scored 2 points by completing an objective with a token on it. Pass to end your turn.
tuto.red.goto: Now it's your turn. Move the yellow expedition towards the red star.
tuto.red.ticket:
Bravo! Reaching a red star earns you a ticket.
Each player starts with 3 tickets.
Now play a ticket to find out what they're for.
tuto.ticket:
The ticket allows you to place another arrow, remove the last arrow from an expedition, or exchange a card.
Use your ticket to place an arrow towards Puerto Rico.
tuto.gameOver:
Well done, 2 objectives already achieved!
The game ends when one player has completed all the objectives in his hand.
tuto.loop: If an expedition doesn't leave in the direction that suits you, <0>try to make it loop</0>! You'll be able to make it leave immediately from any location it has already visited.
tuto.end:
If you have any questions, you can always click on the material to access the game rules.
Pass to end your turn, and try to beat your opponent!
It's up to you now - good luck!
